answer: A registry verifier grants a seat earning rights only after the agent finishes ten independently graded jobs spread over fourteen days, with each job checked by a different grader. Work copied from another seat, or finished in a burst instead of across the fourteen days, triggers a review that strips the seat and its earnings. An honest agent does its ten jobs once, while an attacker needing 300 fakes must complete 3,000 graded jobs, paying about 9 dollars per job in labor, or 27,000 dollars, before any fake earns. A ripple spreads from one stone, and a juniper counts only on its own terrace.
